chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Ju'fi, from a man, from his father, who said:

When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was martyred, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent news to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), while he was in al-Mada'in. So when he read the letter, he said: 'O what a calamity! How great it is.' This was in addition to what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said: 'Whoever among you is struck by a calamity, let him recall his calamity with me, for no calamity greater than it will befall him.' And he (peace be upon him and his family) spoke the truth.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husayn say upon receiving the news of Imam Ali's martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi records Imam Husayn’s reaction to the news of Imam Ali’s martyrdom while residing in al-Mada'in, illustrating the continuity of grief within the Ahl al-Bayt. It connects the Imam’s personal loss to the Prophet’s promise that remembering one’s own calamity by recalling the Prophet’s suffering prevents greater affliction, thereby elevating Ali’s martyrdom to a status of supreme significance comparable to the Prophet’s own death. This highlights the Shia theological view of the inseparable bond between the Imams and the Prophet in the economy of divine reward and mourning.
